headline: Bills Hit Pads, Celebrate Marv Levy's 101st Birthday
writeup: Buffalo Bills training camp hit a significant milestone with the first half-day in pads, as players and coaches embraced the physical step forward under first-year head coach Joe Brady, whose noticeably different approach has caught the attention of the roster. The padded practice came with a pair of injury scares — tight end Dalton Kincaid briefly left the field but quickly returned and humorously confirmed his 'family jewels' were intact, while safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson suffered a more concerning setback, leaving Brady to call the team 'fortunate' as Sam Franklin Jr. stepped into the starting role. Off the injury front, undrafted rookies and depth players like Michael Hoecht were turning heads alongside emerging names in the secondary, with Christian Benford adding a new dimension and DJ Moore settling into his new surroundings, while T.J. Parker's breakout potential drew league-wide attention. Meanwhile, Josh Allen sharpened his game in the rain, navigating Brady's new defensive schemes daily, with analysts and scouts ranking him the NFL's second-best quarterback as expectations for a Super Bowl run build around the roster. Off the field, the old Highmark Stadium continued its demolition as New York State formally took ownership of the gleaming new venue, with Bills legend Jim Kelly among those left stunned by the transformation, and fans eagerly anticipating the Aug. 15 opener.
